currentContext.strengths: Long-standing customer relationships, especially with partners in the Swiss watch industry, described by the Company as a major strength on the export front|Presence across both manufacturing and retail, enabling participation across the luxury value chain with a diversified business portfolio|Eigen focuses on chosen segments requiring high complexity, skills and capabilities along with high entry barriers, and has moved from component supplier to strategic solution provider for global technology leaders|Manufacturing setup equipped to handle complex export requirements, with design capabilities, fast development cycles, shortened response times and competitive pricing|Consistent emphasis on product quality, operational agility and reliability in quality and delivery, which the Company links to tangible market share gains|Eigen's expertise in progressive tool design and die-making, delivering high-speed, zero-defect production for complex assemblies
currentContext.strategies: Stay focused and aligned on premiumisation, supplying high-value, complex-featured watch components tailored to customer requirements|In precision engineering, build relationships with large multinational corporations and high-potential accounts in selected precision component markets, upgrade and add new technical capabilities, expand the product range and extend reach into new geographies|In ornamental packaging, add new customers to serve leading Swiss watchmakers and others, initially for Indian requirements and then leading to global requirements|Make manufacturing excellence a priority, focused on Guaranteed Delivery Dates (GDD), quality and Turnaround Time (TAT)|Pursue strategic marketing initiatives, including an enhanced digital presence to showcase new products and features|Grow precision stamping revenue through market diversification and customer acquisition, backed by a reputation for quality and technical capability|At Pylania SA, build infrastructure and product design capabilities for the manufacture of high-end, precious stone watch dials targeted at premium Swiss watch brands|At Estima AG, invest in strengthening the team, acquire selected machinery for high-quality and complex features and recruit skilled professionals for critical roles, supported by technical guidance from the parent company|At Ethos Limited, shift deliberately towards the luxury and high-luxury segments, scale the certified pre-owned (CPO) business, expand the boutique network, deepen omnichannel capabilities, strengthen the after-sales service vertical and add brand partnerships, with the lifestyle vertical (Messika and Rimowa businesses) reorganised under Ethos Lifestyle Private Limited|Use Kamla International Holdings SA as a special-purpose vehicle for strategic overseas investments
currentContext.expansion: The ornamental packaging division strengthened its capabilities during 2025-26 through the operationalisation of its Panchkula manufacturing facility, which has an installed capacity of approximately 1,00,000 premium boxes per month; capacity utilisation of this new packaging unit in Panchkula, Haryana increased during the year and the division recorded over 35% year-on-year revenue growth on rising domestic demand and a healthy pipeline of RFQs from international brands operating in India. Looking ahead, expanded capacity and the addition of new customers in ornamental packaging are projected to deliver over 25% growth in that segment, while watch component revenue is projected to improve by 10-12% on higher volumes and better realisations. Tangible fixed assets rose during the year, reflecting continued investments in manufacturing infrastructure, capacity enhancement, process improvements and technology upgrades across business segments; loan funds increased to fund capacity expansion, infrastructure development and working capital, and the debt service coverage ratio moderated on higher debt repayments and financing commitments linked to capacity expansion and infrastructure enhancement. In luxury retail, subsidiary Ethos Limited pursued an accelerated pace of boutique expansion, taking its network from 73 to 94 boutiques across 30 cities during the year (103 boutiques across 34 cities as on date), with the lifestyle vertical comprising the Messika and Rimowa businesses reorganised under Ethos Lifestyle Private Limited.

risks.risk: Sustained slowdown in the Swiss watch industry, the Company's core export end-market
risks.note: Swiss watch exports declined 1.7% in value to CHF 25.6 Billion in 2025 with volumes down 4.8% to 14.6 million watches (almost 740,000 fewer watches), a second consecutive year of moderation; the Board reports that the watch component manufacturing business for the Swiss market remained under sustained pressure, with weakness concentrated in China and Hong Kong.

risks.risk: Currency volatility - Rupee weakness and Swiss Franc appreciation
risks.note: The Rupee remained under pressure from a strong US Dollar, elevated US Treasury yields and portfolio outflows and is expected to trade in a broad range of Rs. 92.5-97.0 to the Dollar; the Swiss Franc appreciated over ~23% during the year, crossing Rs. 120 in January 2026, raising imported inventory costs at Ethos Limited and production costs across the Swiss value chain, and the Board lists wide fluctuations in currency among the year's challenges.

risks.risk: Geopolitical conflict, tariffs and protectionism disrupting trade corridors
risks.note: The Board cites geo-political tensions due to wars, tariff issues, a protectionist approach by major markets and regulatory restrictions; the US-Iran war brought additional uncertainty in the Gulf and Middle East with ripple effects in European and Asian markets, and the MD&A notes global growth moderating to 3.1% in 2026 with merchandise trade volume growth slowing to 1.9% on trade policy uncertainty.

risks.risk: Input cost inflation, including precious metals and energy
risks.note: Elevated gold prices increased the cost of Swiss watches; global headline inflation is projected to tick up to 4.4% in 2026, and inflationary risks from global commodity prices, energy markets and geopolitical developments continue to warrant close policy attention.

risks.risk: Customer satisfaction and retention (BRSR material issue, rated a risk with negative financial implications)
risks.note: Customer satisfaction directly affects reputation, customer loyalty and business growth for a watch component and precision engineering company; the Company mitigates through product quality standards, innovation, timely deliveries, competitive pricing, two-way communication channels and a customer-feedback system.

risks.risk: Emissions and energy management (BRSR material issue, rated a risk with negative financial implications)
risks.note: Managing emissions and energy usage is critical for manufacturing; KDDL tracks energy use and emissions through structured policies, encourages adoption of renewable energy including solar and wind, and operates emission tracking systems to monitor significant contributors.

risks.risk: Water management and effluent discharge (BRSR material issue, rated a risk with negative financial implications)
risks.note: The Company mitigates through effluent treatment plants (ETPs) whose treated wastewater is reused for gardening, industrial processes and production, regular monitoring of consumption, and Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) systems operational at three KDDL facilities.

risks.risk: Occupational health and safety, and waste management at manufacturing sites (BRSR material issues, rated risks with negative financial implications)
risks.note: Workplace hazards carry accident, productivity and legal-compliance exposure - mitigated via risk and hazard assessment policies, routine safety audits, health monitoring, PPE, on-site health clinics and safety training; waste is handled, stored and disposed through authorised third-party vendors with reduction and reuse to cut reliance on virgin raw materials.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: KDDL Limited, formerly Kamla Dials and Devices Limited and established in 1981, is headquartered in Chandigarh and operates across India and Switzerland, serving global customers in luxury watchmaking and precision engineering. It manufactures premium watch components - dials, hands, indexes and steel bracelets - for global luxury watch brands, complemented by premium ornamental packaging for watch and jewellery brands, and a precision engineering division (Eigen) making high-precision stamped components and tooling solutions. Through subsidiary Ethos Limited it is present in luxury watch retail, and through Silvercity Brands AG it is rolling out the Favre-Leuba brand internationally.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- The Swiss watch industry is expected to witness gradual stabilisation through 2026 after the moderation of 2025, with recovery visible in select markets while demand in parts of Asia remains measured
- Growth is expected to be supported by continued demand in higher-value segments, with established markets such as the USA providing stability and recovery in key Asian markets an important swing factor
- India is expected to remain one of the most attractive long-term growth markets for Swiss watchmakers, supported by favourable demographics, rising discretionary incomes and the progressive reduction in import duties under TEPA
- Input cost dynamics, including precious metal prices, and currency movements are expected to continue influencing pricing and margins across the value chain
- The Indian watch industry has shifted from volume-driven sales to value-led premiumisation, catalysed by TEPA coming into force on 1st October 2025 and the resulting phased customs duty reduction on Swiss timepieces
- Organised, professionalised luxury retail - larger experiential boutiques, expansion into Tier-II cities and the rise of certified pre-owned - is expected to support demand across the broader luxury watch value chain, including premium packaging and specialised watch components
- The global metal stamping market is transitioning towards high-precision, high-complexity manufacturing driven by the pivot to EVs and miniaturisation in consumer electronics, with China Plus One, Make in India and PLI schemes adding domestic demand for Indian precision manufacturers
- The ornamental packaging market is shifting towards 'Eco-Luxury', while India emerges as an attractive manufacturing destination as global luxury brands diversify supply chains and emphasise localisation, faster turnaround and import substitution
- The domestic watch market is likely to sustain its growth trajectory, offering opportunities to increase market share, with watch component revenue improvement driven by higher volumes and improved average realisations
- At Ethos, margins were affected by the sharp appreciation of the Swiss Franc against the Rupee, which increased the cost of imported inventory, together with higher marketing investment and upfront costs of accelerated boutique expansion
- Ornamental packaging division reported a healthy pipeline of Requests for Quotations (RFQs) from international brands operating in India
- At Estima AG, management remains cautiously optimistic that an improvement in Swiss market conditions will lead to a healthier order pipeline and eventual profitability

capital_allocation.body: Interim dividend: INR15/share declared; capex prioritized for capacity expansion; no M&A announced beyond Favre-Leuba; no share buybacks mentioned

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The ornamental packaging division strengthened its capabilities during 2025-26 through the operationalisation of its Panchkula manufacturing facility, which has an installed capacity of approximately 1,00,000 premium boxes per month; capacity utilisation of this new packaging unit in Panchkula, Haryana increased during the year and the division recorded over 35% year-on-year revenue growth on rising domestic demand and a healthy pipeline of RFQs from international brands operating in India. Looking ahead, expanded capacity and the addition of new customers in ornamental packaging are projected to deliver over 25% growth in that segment, while watch component revenue is projected to improve by 10-12% on higher volumes and better realisations. Tangible fixed assets rose during the year, reflecting continued investments in manufacturing infrastructure, capacity enhancement, process improvements and technology upgrades across business segments; loan funds increased to fund capacity expansion, infrastructure development and working capital, and the debt service coverage ratio moderated on higher debt repayments and financing commitments linked to capacity expansion and infrastructure enhancement. In luxury retail, subsidiary Ethos Limited pursued an accelerated pace of boutique expansion, taking its network from 73 to 94 boutiques across 30 cities during the year (103 boutiques across 34 cities as on date), with the lifestyle vertical comprising the Messika and Rimowa businesses reorganised under Ethos Lifestyle Private Limited.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and proactive; emphasized long-term growth targets, vertical integration, and resilience to short-term tariffs; highlighted execution discipline and flexibility in manufacturing; optimistic on Favre-Leuba and Precision Engineering momentum

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Long-standing customer relationships, especially with partners in the Swiss watch industry, described by the Company as a major strength on the export front
- Presence across both manufacturing and retail, enabling participation across the luxury value chain with a diversified business portfolio
- Eigen focuses on chosen segments requiring high complexity, skills and capabilities along with high entry barriers, and has moved from component supplier to strategic solution provider for global technology leaders
- Manufacturing setup equipped to handle complex export requirements, with design capabilities, fast development cycles, shortened response times and competitive pricing
- Consistent emphasis on product quality, operational agility and reliability in quality and delivery, which the Company links to tangible market share gains
- Eigen's expertise in progressive tool design and die-making, delivering high-speed, zero-defect production for complex assemblies

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: U.S. tariffs on Swiss watches (now reduced to 15%); China/HK luxury demand slowdown; currency volatility; global watch industry cyclicality; execution risk in new capacity ramp-up

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: KDDL's natural forex hedge between export-heavy KDDL and import-heavy Ethos subsidiary; precision stamping for connectors is a hidden high-margin niche supplying Amphenol/TE Connectivity; bracelet expansion uses flexible tech for small-batch production, aligning with luxury industry's shift to agility

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| U.S. 39% tariff on Swiss watches | KDDL Limited | beneficiary | High | Tariff reduced to 15% in Nov 2025, unlocking U.S. demand for Favre-Leuba and precision components |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition/Brand] In 2023 KDDL acquired the iconic Swiss brand Favre-Leuba, with plans for a global relaunch; it is housed in Silvercity Brands AG (93.08%, directly and indirectly through subsidiaries), described as "Business of premium luxury watches under the brand 'Favre Leuba'".
- [Group vs listed entity] Consolidated figures are dominated by the retail subsidiary rather than the components business: FY26 consolidated revenue from operations is Rs 2,153.4 Cr against standalone Rs 495.8 Cr, and FY26 consolidated gross profit margin is 42.2% against standalone 74.9% — the two bases must not be read interchangeably.
- [Regulation] The FY26 consolidated P&L carries an Exceptional Expense of Rs 2.4 Cr, footnoted as "Statutory impact of Labor Codes of Rs. 2.45 Cr" (the deck states 2.4 in the table and 2.45 in the footnote).
- [Historical one-offs] FY24 standalone included an Exceptional Expense of Rs 19.6 Cr, footnoted as an "impairment allowance in the value of investment which is accounted for in other expenses"; FY23 standalone included an Exceptional Expense of Rs 19.0 Cr, footnoted as a "One-time value creation award to Mr. Yashovardhan Saboo (Chairman & MD)". These make the FY23/FY24 standalone PAT and EPS non-comparable with other years.
- [Investor relations] The deck names Sanjeev Masown as CFO of KDDL and Strategic Growth Advisors Limited as the investor-relations advisor.
